content.comment_body: Hello, I have two questions regarding current transducer selection and fuse protection for a [product_name] PLC. 1 - I am working with a DC electric motor that operates from 0 to 40Amps, and I would like to record the current. Could you suggest a reasonably priced current transducer? Most options I found are quite expensive. 2 - I protected my [product_name] module with a 0.8Amp fuse based on the manual's recommendation. However, the manual does not mention protection for inputs. I connect 24V to switch my inputs, but have not added any protective device. Is this a good practice?

Hi [user_name], 1. I am not sure about affordable options for current transducers; I personally use Lem transducers without knowing their cost. 2. There is usually no need to fuse the inputs—as damage won't occur even if a short circuit happens (your wiring and power supply should be fused instead). Output protection is needed due to higher currents in case of shorts. I typically use interface relays for output protection. Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks for your response. I have not protected the output yet. My setup uses outputs to control relays—one relay per output. In this arrangement, do you still think fusing is worth it? I am aiming for a budget-friendly project. If output protection is necessary, can I just use a basic fuse holder with a standard fuse?

If you are only using relays, protection is generally not required, unless the relays are particularly large. In larger cases, I recommend placing a diode in parallel with the relay coil. Best regards, [user_name]

There are few affordable ways to measure motor current. I have been using transformers that measure AC current directly and give a 4-20mA signal output; these typically cost between 70 and 150 EUR depending on the current rating required.

1: [url] 2: You can use the same protection fuse for the power supply and inputs of the [product_name]. This approach is straightforward and incurs no additional cost. Output protection is also advised, even if you're only controlling relays. A burned relay coil can cause damage, so a small glass fuse provides reliable protection at an affordable price.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring practical and affordable protection and current monitoring solutions for [product_name] modules in small automation setups. There's some uncertainty about when and how to fuse inputs and outputs, and users are facing challenges with the high cost of suitable current transducers—especially for applications involving high current. The discussion highlights the tradeoff between keeping costs low and ensuring adequate protection to prevent equipment damage.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking a low-cost way to measure DC motor current and are looking for straightforward guidance on protecting both inputs and outputs of [product_name] modules, favoring solutions that add minimal expense or complexity.
